blocks.content: Grants-in-aid of the revenues of such States as Parliament may determine to be in need of assistance are provided under Article 275 of the Constitution.

rows: Binding upon parliamentary approval based on FC recommendations
Discretionary and optional for specific public purposes
To assist states facing financial distress and reduce regional disparities
To advance specific central schemes and developmental priorities

items: Article 275 covers statutory grants recommended by the Finance Commission, while Article 282 deals with discretionary grants made by the Union.
Tied grants to local bodies must be exclusively spent on national priorities like sanitation, drinking water supply, and rainwater harvesting.
Post-Devolution Revenue Deficit Grants are assessed individually for each state after calculating vertical and horizontal tax transfers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Grants-in-aid are recommended by the Finance Commission under Article 275 of the Constitution of India to meet state revenue deficits.
Revenue Deficit Grants are provided to bridge the post-devolution financial gap in the revenue accounts of needy states.
Local Body Grants are allocated to Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), divided into tied and untied components.
Sector-Specific Grants aim to boost critical social and economic infrastructure such as health, education, and agriculture.
Disaster Relief Grants are assigned to strengthen State Disaster Response Funds (SDRF) and State Disaster Mitigation Funds (SDMF).
